duration: One-time workdays or long-term roles with a yearly minimum of hours
name: Volunteer Programs (teen openings)
org: Forest Preserve District of DuPage County
what_you_do: Volunteer in the forest preserves. Jobs include one-time restoration workdays and special events. You can also help at nature centers, farms and historic sites. Teens 13 to 17 have a few long-term roles.
who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
deadline_text: No single deadline. Some roles have deadlines and limited space. New volunteer orientation is held monthly at district headquarters (second Wednesday evening).
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.
